chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, who said:

Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar sent me to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) as a courtesy. So I entered upon him on a scorching hot day, and in front of him was a tray containing green apples. By Allah, I could not bear it and said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! You are eating from this while people dislike it?' He said to me as if he had not ceased to recognize me: 'I woke up with a chill in this night of mine, so I sent for it and it was brought to me. I ate it, and it removes the fever and calms the heat.' So I returned home and found my family suffering from fever, so I fed them (apples), and the fever was lifted from them.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of green apples in Shia hadith and their medicinal benefits according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in utilizing natural remedies, specifically green apples, to treat fever and heat, countering the contemporary aversion to their taste. The narrative underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the medicinal benefits of food (al-tibb al-taghazuri) as a manifestation of divine knowledge, with the narrator’s successful application of this remedy to his family serving as a testament to its efficacy. It highlights the Imam’s role not only as a spiritual guide but also as a source of practical health knowledge for the community.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Abdullah Bin Sinna, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour who said,

‘Al-Mufazzal Bin Umar sent me to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> as a courtesy. So I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> on a scorching hot day, and facing him<sup>asws</sup> was a tray in which there were green apples, so by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I could not be patient and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> are eating from this and the people are abhorring it?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me as if he<sup>asws</sup> had not ceased to recognise me: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> woke up in this night of mine<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> sent for it and they came with it, So I<sup>asws</sup> ate it and it takes off the fever and settles the temperature’. 
So I proceeded (home) and I found my family with fever, so I fed them (apples), and the fever was lifted from them’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadaniy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Durust ibn abu Mansur who has said the following:

“Al-Mufaddal ibn ’Umar once sent me to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, for a favor (from the Imam). I went to him (the Imam) on a summer day and before him there was a tray with green apples in it and I by Allah could hardly wait until I asked saying, ’I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, do you eat this while people dislike it?’ He (the Imam) said, as if he still remembered me, ’Last night I had a fever so I sent for it and it was brought for me. I ate it and it cuts down the fever and calms down high temperature.’ I returned and found my family with fever. I fed them (such apples) and fever was cut off from them.”
